Decisions this run made

The close calls, and the other reading of each

Every judgment this run flagged as one that could have gone the other way, with what it moved. A grade that rests on one of these is a grade you can overturn: if the other reading is right for your system, say so, and the next run inherits your answer instead of guessing again.

Excluded apps/v4/registry/_legacy-base-colors.ts (1,113 decls), apps/v4/registry/_legacy-colors.ts (1,200 decls), apps/v4/registry/themes.ts (840 decls) and apps/v4/app/legacy-themes.css (439 decls) from the declared token system.
run.token_count from a raw discovery figure of 1,185 concepts down to 40 canonical tokens; single-source, coverage and orphans all graded against the smaller, real system instead of being swamped by catalog data.
single-source · coverage · orphans
All four files are reachable from owned production entry points and declaration-shaped, so a stricter reading of 'discover every candidate, prove it ships' would inventory them as canonical sources the same as globals.css.
Reported a deduplicated, collapsed canonical token count (40) as run.token_count, not the raw discover_tokens.py concept count for globals.css (93) or the theoretical alias_of-is-null count (35).
The headline count away from double-counting Tailwind v4's own '@theme inline' pattern: 53 of the 93 raw concepts are same-file CSS-custom-property aliases (e.g. concept 'primary' and concept 'color-primary', the latter's sole value being 'var(--primary)') that discover_tokens.py's projection-collapse rule does not yet fold into their canonical concept — that rule currently covers only SCSS-to-CSS-custom-property compilation. This run applied that collapse by hand for tokens.filtered.json, merging each alias's site onto its canonical concept as a 'projected_from' entry. chart-1..5 (family 'color') were kept as their own canonical concepts rather than collapsed, because their alias target (--color-blue-300..800) is Tailwind's own default palette, not a name declared in this file — references/vitals.md's framework-default rule counts a project's own reference to a framework default as the project's token. font-sans/font-heading/font-mono were excluded rather than counted, because their @theme-inline declaration is self-referential (alias_of == its own id) — a passthrough for a next/font runtime-injected value, not a static definition.
report
A stricter, literal reading of the tool's own concept list would report 93 (no collapsing) or 35 (collapsing only alias_of-is-null concepts, which would incorrectly also drop chart-1..5).
Excluded 20 'canonical' concepts discover_tokens.py found outside globals.css (apps/v4/lib/font-definitions.ts, hooks/use-meta-color.ts, app/layout.tsx, app/(view)/preview/typeset/layout.tsx, and several font-loader helper files) from the token count.
token_count away from counting non-token JS object properties as design tokens, and stack.token_sources down to the one file the project actually declares its design tokens in.
report
Inspecting each: 'opengraph.width'/'opengraph.height' are literal OpenGraph image pixel dimensions (app/layout.tsx:45-46), 'icons.icon' is a favicon file path (app/layout.tsx:59), 'meta-theme-colors.dark'/'meta-theme-colors.light' are PWA theme-color meta values (hooks/use-meta-color.ts:5-6), and the rest (label/name/title/variable/registryvariable/previewvariable/value) are internal property names inside a custom font-loader's metadata records (lib/font-definitions.ts) — none is a name a component author would type in place of a value. The conservative-js-theme-object extractor currently has no shape heuristic to tell a real token map from an arbitrary data object; this is a tool limitation worth fixing, not a project finding.

mode-completeness to 'pass' with real file:line evidence, instead of 'blocked' — discovery.mode_resolution's own capability stayed unmeasured (the generic engine has no CSS-source-pairing check, only a build/runtime-artifact one), so a strict reading of the vitals.md instruction ('graded only where compiled or resolved output exists') would leave this blocked.
mode-completeness
references/vitals.md's mode-completeness signal is stated as 'the set difference across mode blocks' without requiring compiled output specifically (unlike coverage's framework-default rule, which is explicit about needing a checked version) — reading source blocks directly is a legitimate way to compute that set difference, and the original run against this same repository did the same thing.
The eight vitals

Eight checks on your token system

Each check is graded on its own, against evidence pulled from your repository. There is no single overall score, because averaging these would hide the one thing you need to see. If your system has no dark mode, that check is marked not applicable rather than counted against you. And if a check could not run at all, it says blocked instead of quietly passing.

attention

tier integrity

10 of 485 .tsx files in registry/new-york-v4 (2.1%) use a raw Tailwind palette utility (blue-500, red-600, neutral-200, and similar) where a semantic token already covers the case — every one of them inside registry/new-york-v4/examples/*, files that intentionally demo arbitrary colors (a spinner in five colors, password-strength indicators, toggle/checkbox color variants), not core chrome. 2.1% falls in the >0%-to-5% attention band. registry/new-york-v4/ui/bubble.tsx:29 was checked and excluded — its bg-[oklch(from_var(--primary)_...)] values derive from var(--primary), which references/adapters/tailwind.md says clears the bar; only bare literals count. apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/examples/spinner-color.tsx:6

pass

leakage

audit_literal_colors.py scanned 13 owned reachable consumer stylesheets and found zero redundant and zero exact-value-candidate findings; leakage's pass/attention/fail line reads only the redundant tier (references/vitals.md), so the mechanical grade is pass. Two real uncovered findings still exist (not in fix_queue — an uncovered finding has no replacement token to queue): #000000 x24 in the CLI's shipped packages/shadcn/src/tailwind.css, and #378ADD x3 (one literal, three near-identical demo files) in a Tailwind bracket-arbitrary class the generic scanner does not check (registry/new-york-v4/examples/{aria,base,radix}/shimmer-color.tsx:7). near-miss stayed unmeasured for color, and 214 further Tailwind bracket-arbitrary px/rem literals across registry/new-york-v4 were found but not individually reviewed — see decisions. packages/shadcn/src/tailwind.css:170

attention

coverage

9 of 11 categories present. color, typography, space, size, radius, border, elevation, motion and breakpoint all resolve to a real token — either a project token in globals.css, or one of Tailwind v4's own default-theme tokens the project imports and never overrides (verified against tailwindcss@4.3.0, the exact version pinned in pnpm-lock.yaml). z-index and opacity do not: Tailwind v4 ships no --z-* or --opacity-* default theme scale, so z-50 and opacity-50 compile to fixed values with nothing for a component author to reach for instead. 9/11 falls in the 8-10 attention band. apps/v4/app/layout.tsx

pass

mode completeness

Every color-family token declared in :root (light, starting line 99) is redefined in .dark (starting line 143): background, foreground, card, popover, primary, secondary, muted, accent, destructive, border, input, ring, chart-1..5, all 8 sidebar tokens, surface, code/code-foreground, code-highlight, code-number, selection, selection-foreground — zero gaps. The one property in :root absent from .dark is --radius (globals.css:100), a corner-radius value; .dark applies as an additional class alongside :root rather than replacing it, and references/vitals.md scopes mode-completeness to appearance-dependent tokens, putting geometry out of scope by default — the same judgment call the original run made. chart-1..5 resolve to the identical Tailwind-default value in both blocks, so the chart palette itself does not shift with the mode; that is a deliberate constant, not a gap. This grade comes from an agent reading both CSS blocks directly, not from a tool-verified compiled artifact — discovery.mode_resolution's own capability stayed unmeasured — see decisions. apps/v4/app/globals.css:99

pass

naming coherence

Every one of the 40 canonical tokens and the same-file aliases/projections that build on them follows one grammar: a kebab-case role name, optionally suffixed -foreground for the paired on-color text (accent/accent-foreground, sidebar-accent/sidebar-accent-foreground, and so on). No second grammar or legacy family found within the declared scope. apps/v4/app/globals.css:99

pass

single source

Within the declared scope (globals.css), every one of the 40 canonical concepts has exactly one definition site. apps/v4/registry/themes.ts and apps/v4/app/legacy-themes.css do redeclare the same names (chart-1..5 and others) with alternate values, but those are the theme-gallery/legacy-preview catalog this run scoped out as content rather than the site's own applied system — see decisions[0]. That exclusion is what changed this grade from the original run's attention. apps/v4/app/globals.css:99

pass

orphans

Checked all 55 declared token names (40 canonical + the remaining same-file aliases not folded into a parent, such as the individual @theme-inline color-* projection names) for at least one reference in apps/v4, combining two search forms: a Tailwind-utility-class grep (bg-x, text-x, border-x, and so on) across registry/new-york-v4, components, app, examples, hooks and lib, and a direct var(--x)/pseudo-selector grep against every reachable file including globals.css itself. The utility-class search alone showed 4 apparent zero-hit names — code-highlight, code-number, selection, selection-foreground — and all four turned out to be used, just not via a Tailwind class: selection/selection-foreground back the ::selection rule at globals.css:195, and code-highlight/code-number are consumed via direct var(--color-code-highlight)/var(--color-code-number) CSS at globals.css:365,372,426 (rehype-pretty-code line-highlighting). No orphaned token found.

blocked

enforcement

No lint rule or CI gate in this repository reads the token layer. apps/v4/eslint.config.mjs runs eslint-config-next plus typescript-eslint scoped to type-import style and React hooks correctness — nothing about colors, spacing, or bracket-arbitrary literals. No stylelint config exists anywhere in the repository. .github/workflows/code-check.yml runs pnpm lint / format:check / typecheck; .github/workflows/monitor-registries.yml checks registry health (broken imports, stale exports), not token usage. 0 qualifying rules found, so per the vital's own grading this is blocked rather than failed.

Pass — checked, nothing to fix Attention — worth a look, not urgent Fail — real problems with a clear fix Blocked — could not check this one N/A — does not apply to your setup

Orphans & enforcement

Tokens nothing uses, and what stops this coming back

Orphaned tokens make your system look bigger and more capable than it really is. They stick around because nothing breaks when they go, so nobody ever gets a reason to remove them.

Orphan measurement

pass

Checked all 55 declared token names (40 canonical + the remaining same-file aliases not folded into a parent, such as the individual @theme-inline color-* projection names) for at least one reference in apps/v4, combining two search forms: a Tailwind-utility-class grep (bg-x, text-x, border-x, and so on) across registry/new-york-v4, components, app, examples, hooks and lib, and a direct var(--x)/pseudo-selector grep against every reachable file including globals.css itself. The utility-class search alone showed 4 apparent zero-hit names — code-highlight, code-number, selection, selection-foreground — and all four turned out to be used, just not via a Tailwind class: selection/selection-foreground back the ::selection rule at globals.css:195, and code-highlight/code-number are consumed via direct var(--color-code-highlight)/var(--color-code-number) CSS at globals.css:365,372,426 (rehype-pretty-code line-highlighting). No orphaned token found.

What protects this today

monorepo investigation guide
import_resolutionResolve workspace package names to source directories before calling them external.
mode_resolutionAudit bundle-by-scheme output for the selected app only.
ownershipRecord the selected app and which workspace packages it owns or consumes.
production_rootsIdentify application candidates and require a selection when several could change scope.
runtime_verificationRun or build the selected app, not an arbitrary workspace package.
token_source_discoveryTrace shared token packages from the selected application rather than inventorying every workspace.
nextjs investigation guide
import_resolutionFollow JS/TS, dynamic and CSS-module imports using tsconfig/jsconfig aliases and workspace packages.
mode_resolutionInspect each route shell and theme-provider path; declarations alone do not prove rendered values.
ownershipKeep Storybook, generated .next output and external workspace packages outside product scope unless selected.
production_rootsCompose root layouts, _app, filesystem routes, global CSS and route-local CSS modules.
runtime_verificationUse built or rendered routes for every declared scheme when available.
token_source_discoveryInspect global CSS, CSS modules, theme providers, JS/TS theme objects and framework configuration.
Measurement

How this was measured

Two runs against the same repository should be able to agree, or at least explain why they don't. This is what makes that possible: the exact sources this run counted as tokens, the scope and file count it searched for leaks, the adapters it detected and how sure it was, and any framework version it had to check before grading coverage. Recorded here, a difference between two runs points at a fact instead of an argument.

Measured scope

2 profiles proved 31 product roots: 31 owned and 0 unresolved in ownership. The full graph reaches 3314 files; the owned graph reaches 3314. 5837 imports remain classified, 40 canonical concepts came from 1 reachable token-bearing sources, and 35 candidate or override sources were held out.
